sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.body: Users receive the ORN-503 error when logging into Orion ERP or order screens hang for more than 60 seconds. The Zabbix monitor triggers the ERP-HEALTH alert in red.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.body: Check the status of the orion-app service on the erp-app-01 and erp-app-02 nodes with systemctl status orion-app. Review the database connection pool: if it exceeds 180 out of 200 connections, the bottleneck is the database and not the application.

sections.heading: Recovery
sections.body: Restart the node with the highest memory usage first, never both at the same time. If the error persists after two restarts, activate contingency mode: orders are captured in the backup sheet and loaded with the ORN-IMPORT job upon service restoration.

sections.heading: Scaling
sections.body: If the outage lasts more than 30 minutes, a P1 incident is declared and a case is opened with OrionSoft according to the SLA-D. The on-call manager notifies sales and the distribution centers.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.body: Branch offices lose access to ERP and WMS simultaneously, while local internet remains functional. The border router rt-core-01 shows the interface Gi0/1 in a down state.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.body: Ping the NetLink gateway at 10.20.0.1 and execute traceroute from rt-core-01. If the last responding hop is the provider's equipment, the failure is on NetLink's side.

sections.heading: Switch to Secondary Link
sections.body: Traffic reroutes through the IPsec tunnel over Telcom Express internet link (SLA-A). The switch occurs automatically via BGP within less than 3 minutes; if it does not occur, manually lower the MPLS route priority using the command documented in the network appendix.

sections.heading: Report to Provider
sections.body: Open a ticket with NetLink at 800-555-0142 indicating the MPLS circuit ID MPLS-NL-7781. The SLA-B contract obliges NetLink to respond within 30 minutes for total outages.

sections.heading: When to Apply
sections.body: Use this procedure when dockside radio-frequency terminals cannot confirm picks or Atlas WMS takes more than 10 seconds to respond to a scan.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.body: Notify shift supervisors to pause picking. Stop the atlas-core service, clear the message queue with purge_queue.sh, and restart it. A full restart takes approximately 7 minutes.

sections.heading: Validation
sections.body: Confirm that the pending task queue returns to zero and perform a test scan at platform 1. Record the start and end times in the ticket.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Applies to the PostgreSQL database db-fact-01 that stores electronic invoices and credit notes.

sections.heading: Available Backups
sections.body: There is a full daily backup at 02:00 and WAL archiving every 5 minutes in CloudVault (SLA-I). This allows recovery to a point-in-time with a maximum data loss of 5 minutes.

sections.heading: Restoration Procedure
sections.body: Restore the latest full backup to a clean server, apply the WALs up to the desired time using recovery_target_time, and validate invoice counts against the SAT portal before redirecting the application.

sections.heading: Authorization
sections.body: All production restorations require approval from the finance leader and an emergency change registered according to POL-03.

sections.heading: Indicators
sections.body: A user reports a suspicious email in which they entered their password, or the email system detects login attempts from another country.

sections.heading: Immediate Containment
sections.body: Disable the account, revoke all active sessions, and enforce password and second factor reset. Block the malicious email sender and domain in the filter.

sections.heading: Investigation
sections.body: Review forwarding rules created in the mailbox, access logs from the last 14 days, and shared file downloads. Preserve evidence in the incident folder.

sections.heading: Notification
sections.body: If there was access to information classified as Confidential according to POL-08, the security officer notifies the address within a maximum of 24 hours.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.body: Zebra ZT411 thermal printers print labels in white, misaligned, or do not receive jobs from the WMS.

sections.heading: Quick Fix
sections.body: Recalibrate the media sensor by holding down the pause and cancel buttons for 2 seconds. If printing in white, check that the roll is thermal transfer and not direct thermal.

sections.heading: Print Queue
sections.body: If jobs are not arriving, check the PRN-ANDEN print queue on the print server and restart the spooler service. Replacement printers are located in the IT warehouse, shelf 4.

documents.title: Inventory Desynchronization Between WMS and ERP

sections.heading: Problem Description
sections.body: The available inventory in ERP Orion does not match the stock levels in WMS Atlas. This is a known issue registered as T-1042 and typically appears after month-end closures with high volume.

sections.heading: Known Root Cause
sections.body: The INV-SYNC interface job stops processing when it receives an SKU with more than 18 characters and stops processing subsequent movements without marking an error.

sections.heading: Resolution
sections.body: Identify the problematic SKU in the INV-SYNC log, correct it in the item master, and restart the job with the --desde-ultimo-ok option. Then run the reconciliation report CONC-02 to confirm that the differences are zero.

sections.heading: Prevention
sections.body: Since March 2026, the item master validates the SKU length. The ticket T-1042 remains open until the vendor releases the definitive patch.

sections.heading: Alerts
sections.body: Monitoring alerts 30 days prior to the expiration of any public certificate and re-alerts with priority P2 7 days before expiration.

sections.heading: Renewal
sections.body: Customer portal certificates are issued by DigiCert using the corporate account. Generate the CSR with a minimum RSA key size of 2048 bits and upload it to the provider's portal.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.body: Install the certificate and intermediate chain on the load balancer lb-ext-01 and verify with an external SSL test that the rating is A or higher.

sections.heading: Thresholds
sections.body: An alert is triggered at 80% disk usage and is considered critical at 90%.

sections.heading: Safe Cleanup
sections.body: Compress and move logs older than 7 days from /var/log/apps to cold storage. Never delete files from /data/spool as they contain pending transactions to be sent.

sections.heading: Expansion
sections.body: If disk usage remains above 80% after cleanup, request volume expansion from the infrastructure team using a standard change process.

sections.heading: Symptoms
sections.body: Remote users are unable to connect to the GW-VPN-02 concentrator or are disconnected every few minutes.

sections.heading: Diagnosis
sections.body: Check if the number of active tunnels has reached the 250 simultaneous user license limit and if the VPN portal certificate is still valid.

sections.heading: Temporary Solution
sections.body: Enable the alternate concentrator GW-VPN-03 and inform users of the alternate address vpn2.operadora.example. Prioritize access for finance and the service desk.

documents.title: Power Outage at the Data Center

sections.heading: Initial Response
sections.body: Upon detecting the outage, the UPS supports the load for up to 15 minutes. The diesel generator must start automatically within less than 30 seconds; if it fails to start, the on-site DataCenter Monterrey technician must manually ignite it.

sections.heading: Ordered Shutdown
sections.body: If the generator is unavailable and the UPS drops below 40% load, shut down the test environments first, followed by applications, and finally the databases.

sections.heading: Recovery
sections.body: Upon restoring power, power up in reverse order: storage, databases, applications, and finally user services. Validate the integrity of the databases before resuming operations.

sections.heading: Request
sections.body: Human Resources sends the ALTA-01 form at least 3 business days in advance of the start date.

sections.heading: Base Access
sections.body: Every employee receives email, VPN, and read-only access to the documentation portal. Role-based Orion ERP access requires approval from the employee's manager.

sections.heading: Delivery
sections.body: The service desk delivers credentials in person or via call, never by email. The user must activate MFA on the first day according to POL-02.

sections.heading: Service Scope
sections.body: Telcom Express provides a dedicated 200 Mbps internet link at the data center, used as a backup for NetLink's MPLS.

sections.heading: Availability
sections.body: Monthly committed availability of 99.5 %. Maintenance windows are announced with 5 days' notice.

sections.heading: Response Times
sections.body: Response within 1 hour and resolution within 8 hours for total outages. 24x7 telephone support at 800-555-0199.

sections.heading: Service Scope
sections.body: NetLink provides the MPLS network connecting the data center to 14 branch offices and 3 distribution centers.

sections.heading: Availability
sections.body: Monthly committed availability of 99.7 % per circuit, measured by the provider's monitoring and validated against ours.

sections.heading: Response and Resolution Times
sections.body: Complete failure: response within 30 minutes and resolution within 4 hours. Degradation: response within 2 hours and resolution within 12 hours.

sections.heading: Penalties
sections.body: For each full hour exceeding the resolution time, 5 % of the monthly rental for the circuit is deducted, with a maximum of 30 %. The claim must be made within 15 natural days following the end of the month.

sections.heading: Infrastructure
sections.body: Two 42U racks with redundant power A+B, UPS, and generator with 48 hours of diesel autonomy.

sections.heading: Physical Access
sections.body: Physical access requires prior registration in the provider's portal with 24 hours advance notice; for emergencies, the on-call manager may authorize via phone.

sections.heading: Commitments
sections.body: 99.98 % energy availability. Cold aisle temperature between 18 and 27 degrees. On-site technician with 15 minute response time for remote hands.

sections.heading: Coverage
sections.body: Application and database support for the Orion ERP; includes patches and minor updates.

sections.heading: Priorities and Response Times
sections.body: P1: Response within 1 hour, 24x7. P2: Response within 4 business hours. P3 and P4: Next business day.

sections.heading: Contact Channel
sections.body: Cases are opened via the support.orionsoft.example portal with the customer number OR-55120. P1 cases are also confirmed by phone.

sections.heading: Hours
sections.body: Support available Monday to Saturday from 7:00 to 22:00. Calls outside of these hours are routed to the on-call internal engineer.

sections.heading: Metrics
sections.body: First Contact Resolution in at least 70 % of cases and minimum satisfaction of 4.2 out of 5 in the monthly survey.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Password reset, device configuration, office printers, and user onboarding. Does not handle server or network failures.

sections.heading: Preventive Maintenance
sections.body: Each elevator receives preventive service every 250 hours of operation or every 3 months, whichever occurs first.

sections.heading: Failures
sections.body: For a stopped elevator, MontaServ must arrive within 4 hours in metropolitan areas and 8 hours in remote locations. If the repair exceeds 48 hours, a replacement unit must be provided.

sections.heading: Penalties
sections.body: Each day without replacement after 48 hours incurs a penalty of 2,000 MXN per unit.

sections.heading: Delivery Times
sections.body: Local deliveries within 24 hours and out-of-area deliveries within 48 hours from pickup at the distribution center.

sections.heading: Metrics
sections.body: On-time delivery rate of at least 95 % monthly and damage rate below 0.5 % of packages.

sections.heading: Non-Compliance
sections.body: If the on-time delivery rate drops below 95 % for two consecutive months, a contract review is triggered according to POL-09.

sections.heading: Coverage
sections.body: 24x7 guards at the three distribution centers and patrols every 2 hours in the trailer parking lot.

sections.heading: Access Control
sections.body: All visitors register with official identification and receive a temporary badge. Carriers wait in the booth until the assigned dock is available.

sections.heading: Incident Reporting
sections.body: VigiPro provides a written report of any incident within less than 2 hours and a monthly summary with statistics.

sections.heading: Service
sections.body: Encrypted backup storage using AES-256 across two distinct geographic regions.

sections.heading: Retention
sections.body: Daily backups are retained for 35 days and monthly backups for 12 months, aligned with POL-05.

sections.heading: Restoration
sections.body: Backup download initiation time less than 1 hour. Quarterly restoration tests with signed evidence from both parties.

sections.heading: Priorities
sections.body: P1: Operation halted at one or more distribution centers or critical system down. P2: Severe degradation with manual alternative. P3: Affects a user or area without halting operation. P4: Requests and inquiries.

sections.heading: Internal Target Times
sections.body: P1 response within 15 minutes and status communication every 30 minutes. P2 within 1 hour. P3 within 8 business hours.

sections.heading: Roles
sections.body: Each P1 has an Incident Coordinator who leads the call and a Business Communication Owner. Neither of the two may execute technical changes.

sections.heading: Closure
sections.body: An P1 or P2 incident closes only when the user confirms service restoration and the postmortem is scheduled according to POL-11.

sections.heading: Password Requirements
sections.body: Minimum 14 characters, no periodic expiration unless suspected compromise. The account is locked for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts.

sections.heading: Second Factor
sections.body: MFA is required for email, VPN, ERP Orion, and administration consoles. Authenticator app or physical key are accepted; SMS is not permitted.

sections.heading: Service Accounts
sections.body: Service accounts use 32-character passwords stored in the secret vault and are rotated every 180 days.

sections.heading: Change Types
sections.body: Standard: pre-approved and low-risk. Normal: requires CAB committee approval. Emergency: approved by the on-call manager and documented within the following 48 hours.

sections.heading: Maintenance Windows
sections.body: Normal changes are executed on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 23:00 to 03:00. No changes are allowed from the 28th to the 3rd of each month due to the closing period.

sections.heading: CAB Committee
sections.body: The CAB meets every Monday at 10:00. Requests must be registered before Friday at 14:00 with a proven rollback plan.

sections.heading: Rotation
sections.body: Shifts are weekly, from Monday 09:00 to Monday 09:00, with a primary and a secondary engineer.

sections.heading: Response Times
sections.body: The primary must acknowledge the alert within 10 minutes. If not, the platform automatically escalates to the secondary and then to the on-call manager.

sections.heading: Compensation
sections.body: Each week of on-call duty is compensated with a fixed bonus equivalent to 2 days of salary, plus overtime for interventions outside of working hours exceeding 30 minutes. A day off is granted after a night shift with more than 3 hours of work.

sections.heading: Retention Periods
sections.body: Daily: 35 days. Monthly: 12 months. Annual fiscal information: 5 years.

sections.heading: Testing
sections.body: At least one critical system is restored quarterly in an isolated environment, and the real-time recovery time is documented.

sections.heading: Responsibilities
sections.body: The infrastructure team operates the backups; the owner of each system validates the restoration test.

sections.heading: Assigned Equipment
sections.body: Laptops are company property and are delivered with full disk encryption. It is prohibited to install unlicensed software or disable the antivirus.

sections.heading: Personal Use
sections.body: Reasonable personal use is permitted as long as it does not interfere with operations or involve storing company information in personal cloud services.

sections.heading: Loss or Theft
sections.body: Report loss or theft to the service desk within less than 4 hours to remotely lock and wipe the device.

sections.heading: Amounts
sections.body: Meals up to 650 MXN per day in metropolitan areas and 900 MXN for out-of-town travel. Accommodation up to 1,800 MXN per night.

sections.heading: Reimbursement
sections.body: Expenses are reimbursed with an electronic invoice in the company's name within 5 business days following return.

sections.heading: Exceptions
sections.body: Expenses exceeding the limit require prior approval from the operations manager via email.

sections.heading: Levels
sections.body: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Contracts with vendors and customer data are Confidential; payroll and cryptographic keys are Restricted.

sections.heading: Handling
sections.body: Confidential information is shared only with corporate accounts and never on unencrypted USB drives. Restricted information requires approval from the information owner for each access.

sections.heading: Labeling
sections.body: All Confidential or Restricted documents carry the level label in the header.

sections.heading: Quarterly Evaluation
sections.body: Each critical vendor is evaluated quarterly on a 1-to-5 scale for SLA compliance, quality, and communication.

sections.heading: Critical Vendors
sections.body: The following are considered critical: NetLink, OrionSoft, DataCenter Monterrey, CloudVault, and RutaVeloz.

sections.heading: Improvement Plan
sections.body: A rating below 3 requires a 60-day improvement plan. Two consecutive quarters below 3 trigger a search for an alternative vendor.

sections.heading: System Objectives
sections.body: ERP Orion: RTO 4 hours and RPO 15 minutes. WMS Atlas: RTO 2 hours and RPO 5 minutes. Email: RTO 8 hours and RPO 1 hour.

sections.heading: Alternate Site
sections.body: The alternate site in the cloud is activated at the discretion of the operations director when it is estimated that the data center will be unavailable for more than 6 hours.

sections.heading: Drills
sections.body: A business continuity drill is conducted every semester with participation from IT, operations, and finance.

sections.heading: When Required
sections.body: All P1 incidents and all P2 incidents lasting more than 4 hours require a postmortem.

sections.heading: Timeline and Format
sections.body: The document is published within a maximum of 5 business days and includes timeline, root cause, impact, and corrective actions with responsible party and due date.

sections.heading: Blameless Focus
sections.body: The analysis focuses on processes and systems, not on individuals. Corrective actions are reviewed during the weekly operations meeting until closure.
